questions: Q1: Are the two new CLI handlers (hlx inspect netsuite, hlx run) correctly implemented as thin interfaces to the server-side endpoints?
Q2: Does the CLI correctly handle environment selection via --env with manifest-based defaults?

answers.answer: Yes. netsuite.ts (60 lines) supports two modes: query (POST type='query' with query string) and logs (POST type='logs' with optional scriptId). run/index.ts (53 lines) supports --repo (required), --env/--code/--modules (optional). Both follow existing hxFetch + switch-based routing patterns from db.ts and logs.ts.
evidence: src/inspect/index.ts lines 125-138 — netsuite case in switch verified
src/index.ts lines 101-105 — run case in switch verified

answers.answer: Yes. Both handlers read /tmp/helix-inspect/manifest.json for nsDefaultEnv. Mapping: PRODUCTION->'prod', else->'sandbox'. The --env flag overrides the default. This matches the ticket requirement: per-step default applies when omitted, caller may override.
evidence: src/run/index.ts lines 7-18 — same manifest reading and env mapping

statement: The helix-cli changes are a thin interface layer (~4 files, ~113 lines of new code) that correctly surfaces the server-side ns-gm decomposition. Two new handlers (cmdNetsuite, cmdRun) follow existing CLI patterns, read environment defaults from the inspection manifest, and POST to the server-side endpoints. No gaps identified.
